Shanghai oncology drug maker behind furmonertinib (Aflory, also known as alflutinib), a third-generation EGFR inhibitor approved in China for EGFR-mutant non-small-cell lung cancer. Revenue comes from selling the drug to Chinese hospitals, largely through the national reimbursement list, with licensing to partners such as ArriVent for markets outside China. Listed on Shanghai's STAR market. B2B pharma with no consumer brand; known to oncologists rather than the public.

California immuno-oncology biotech (ARMO BioSciences) whose lead candidate was pegilodecakin (AM0010), a pegylated form of interleukin-10 tested with chemotherapy in pancreatic cancer and other tumours. Pre-revenue, based in Redwood City and Palo Alto, and funded by venture capital and a 2018 Nasdaq IPO. Eli Lilly acquired it in 2018 for about $1.6 billion. B2B biotech, no consumer brand.

New Jersey oncology company whose lead product was Vyxeos (CPX-351), a fixed-ratio liposomal combination of daunorubicin and cytarabine for acute myeloid leukemia, based on its CombiPlex drug-ratio technology. Approved in the US in 2017 after Jazz Pharmaceuticals acquired it in 2016 for about $1.5 billion. Nasdaq listed before the deal. Sold to hospitals and oncologists; no consumer brand. B2B pharma.

Indian irrigation and agri-processing group, based in Jalgaon, Maharashtra, making drip and sprinkler irrigation systems, PVC and polyethylene pipes, plastic sheets, solar pumps, and processed fruit and vegetable products such as mango pulp, onion flakes and dried fruit. Sells to farmers, distributors, governments and food companies, with manufacturing in India and several other countries; among the largest micro-irrigation companies globally. Listed on NSE and BSE. B2B/farmer brand, rural visibility in India.

California device maker behind UroLift, a minimally invasive treatment for enlarged prostate (benign prostatic hyperplasia) in which small implants lift prostate tissue away from the urethra, usually in an outpatient setting. Sold to urologists and hospitals, mainly in the US. Teleflex acquired it in 2017 for about $1.1 billion, and UroLift is now a Teleflex brand. B2B, though marketed to patients directly.

Arizona operator of urgent care and occupational medicine clinics across several US states, including NextCare Urgent Care sites in Arizona, Texas, Colorado, Georgia and others. Patients walk in for minor illness and injury, while employers pay for workers' compensation care, drug testing and occupational health services; insurers and employers provide most revenue. Private equity owned. Local consumer-facing clinic brands, little national awareness.

UK stem cell biotech (Bridgend, Wales) with cell therapy for stroke and retinal disease. Its lead programmes were the CTX stem cell line for stroke disability and human retinal progenitor cells for retinitis pigmentosa, plus exosome work. Pre-revenue and funded through share placings. Listed on AIM. B2B, little public brand awareness.

Cambridge, Massachusetts biotech developing stem-cell-derived islet cells for diabetes, replacing the insulin-producing beta cells lost in type 1 diabetes, with encapsulation devices to avoid immune rejection. Co-founded by Douglas Melton of Harvard. Vertex acquired it in 2019 for about $950 million and continued the work. B2B, no consumer brand.

Cambridge, Massachusetts biotech whose lead candidate Vicineum (oportuzumab monatox), an intravesical fusion protein for BCG-unresponsive non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer, received an FDA complete response letter in 2021. Pre-revenue, funded by equity raises and licensing partners in China and the Middle East. Nasdaq listed (SESN); merged with Carisma Therapeutics in 2023. B2B biotech, no consumer visibility.

Ohio pharma company known for Spritam (levetiracetam), the first FDA-approved 3D-printed drug (2015), which uses ZipDose technology to produce a porous tablet that dissolves rapidly with a sip of liquid. Spritam treats epilepsy seizures and is aimed especially at patients who struggle to swallow pills. Revenue from prescription sales and a contract manufacturing and development service for other drug makers. Based in Mason, Ohio. B2B pharma, with attention in healthcare and technology press.

Chennai-based Indian chemical producer, one of the largest exporters of bromine and industrial salt (marine chemicals), also making sulphate of potash. Its salt works are at Hajipir in the Rann of Kutch, Gujarat, selling to pharma, agrochemical and flame-retardant makers in Asia and elsewhere. Listed on NSE and BSE since 2021. B2B.

Colorado genomics firm with Anchored Multiplex PCR (AMP) technology for next-generation sequencing, used in cancer research and diagnostics, including fusion-gene detection and its FusionPlex and VariantPlex panels. Customers included academic centers, biopharma companies developing companion diagnostics, and clinical labs. Invitae acquired it in 2020 for about $1.4 billion. B2B life sciences, little consumer profile.

Israeli computational drug discovery company in Holon, listed on Nasdaq as CGEN, using its predictive discovery platform to identify immuno-oncology targets and antibodies. Pipeline includes COM701 (anti-PVRIG) and other checkpoint candidates, with partnerships including Bayer and AstraZeneca. Revenue is mostly milestone and licensing payments, not product sales. B2B biotech with little consumer visibility.

California immuno-oncology biotech whose lead candidate was magrolimab, an anti-CD47 antibody that blocks the 'don't eat me' signal on cancer cells, tested in myelodysplastic syndrome and acute myeloid leukemia. Based in Menlo Park, Nasdaq listed (FTSV) before Gilead acquired it in 2020 for about $4.9 billion. Pre-revenue; no consumer brand. B2B biotech.

Beijing precision oncology company (Genetron Health) offering cancer genetic testing, including tumour profiling for treatment selection and early detection tests such as its HCCscreen liver cancer assay, plus companion diagnostics and services to pharma. Customers are hospitals, doctors and biopharma firms across China. Nasdaq listed (GTH). B2B and hospitals; known in oncology circles, little consumer awareness.

Brazilian pharmacy chain based in Fortaleza, one of the largest in the country by stores, strongest in the north and northeast, with Extrafarma acquired in 2016. It sells prescription and generic medicines, beauty and personal care products to consumers, in stores and via an online delivery offer. Listed on B3 since 2020 (PGMN3). Consumer retail brand with solid Brazilian awareness.

Israeli biopharma in Carmiel making recombinant proteins in plant cells (ProCellEx platform), with Elelyso (taliglucerase alfa), an enzyme replacement therapy for Gaucher disease, partnered with Pfizer and Brazil. Pipeline includes PRX-102 (pegunigalsidase alfa) for Fabry disease, licensed to Chiesi. Revenue from Elelyso supply and licensing. Listed on NYSE American as PLX and on the Tel Aviv exchange. B2B.

Cell therapy company that sells MACI, an implant made from a patient's own cartilage cells to repair knee cartilage defects, and Epicel, cultured skin grafts for severe burns. Customers are orthopaedic surgeons and burn centres, with annual revenue of around 200 million dollars. Originally Cambridge, Massachusetts (formerly Aastrom Biosciences); now based in Ann Arbor, Michigan. Listed on Nasdaq as VCEL. B2B with little consumer brand.

Philadelphia agricultural technology company whose SmartFresh product (1-MCP, 1-methylcyclopropene) delays ripening and extends shelf life of apples, pears and other fruit, supplemented by RipeLock and coating products. Customers are fruit growers, packers and storage operators in dozens of countries, with revenue from chemical treatments and equipment. Became public through a 2015 SPAC merger. Listed on Nasdaq as AGFS; taken private by Paine Schwartz in 2023. B2B agri, no consumer brand.

Kenyan cement producer in Nairobi (Athi River), among the largest in East Africa, with the Rhino Cement brand. It also ran a clinker plant at Kaloleni and a Tanzanian limestone subsidiary, selling bagged cement through distributors and hardware dealers to builders and contractors. Listed on the Nairobi Securities Exchange and put into administration in 2018. B2B and construction trade, Rhino a recognised name in Kenyan building.

California maker of flow cytometry instruments (Aurora spectral analysers, Northern Lights, Aurora CS cell sorter) used by life science researchers. Also sells reagents and software, with customers across universities, hospitals, biopharma and clinical labs worldwide. Its full-spectrum technology allows many markers to be read in a single sample. Based in Fremont, California. Listed on Nasdaq as CTKB. B2B with strong scientific reputation but no consumer visibility.

Phoenix cannabis operator (TILT Holdings) that makes vaporiser hardware and cannabis brands (Jupiter Research, Standard Farms) and runs retail in several states. Its Jupiter unit supplies vape hardware and extraction products to cannabis brands, while Standard Farms makes branded product in Pennsylvania, alongside retail in several states. Listed on CSE. Cannabis marketing limits.

New York radiopharma Actinium Pharmaceuticals developing Iomab-B, an antibody-radiation conjugate (apamistamab I-131) for conditioning patients before bone marrow transplant in relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia, with the SIERRA phase 3 trial. Also develops actinium-225 programs such as Actimab-A. Pre-revenue; income from licensing and funding. Listed on NYSE American (ATNM). B2B, known to oncologists and investors, not consumers.

Florida real estate lender focused on cannabis operators (Advanced Flower Capital), formerly AFC Gamma, a REIT on Nasdaq as AFCG. It originates senior secured loans to licensed US cannabis cultivators and dispensary groups, backed by real estate and equipment, and pays out most income as dividends. Externally managed by AFC Management. Revenue from loan interest. Cannabis finance niche, known to investors rather than consumers.

Sheffield-based UK life sciences group providing genetics for aquaculture (shrimp, salmon) and animal health and nutrition, listed on AIM as BMK. Operates through Benchmark Genetics (salmon eggs and shrimp broodstock), Benchmark Animal Health (vaccines and treatments) and Benchmark Biologics, selling to producers, feed companies and vets in dozens of countries. B2B with little consumer awareness.

UK flooring retailer based in Orpington with several hundred stores selling carpets, beds and wood flooring. Customers are household consumers across the UK, shopping in out-of-town and high-street stores and online, with fitted-carpet installation services. Listed on LSE, went into administration in 2024 and was bought by Tapi. Consumer retail brand with UK high-street awareness.

California aesthetic laser maker (excel V, truSculpt, enlighten) selling to dermatology clinics and medspas globally. Its systems treat skin rejuvenation, body contouring, vascular lesions and tattoo removal, with revenue from system sales, consumables and service contracts, via a direct sales force and distributors in dozens of countries. Listed on Nasdaq as CUTR; filed Chapter 11 in 2025. B2B with spa clinic brand reach.

California molecular diagnostics firm (GenMark) with ePlex panels that test patient samples for respiratory, bloodstream and gastrointestinal infections in hours. Sold as an instrument plus consumables to hospital and reference labs, with revenue from cartridge sales. Roche acquired it in 2021 for about $1.8 billion. B2B.

Pennsylvania maker and distributor of hydroponic growing equipment and nutrients for indoor farmers and cannabis growers, with brands like Phantom and Active Aqua. Products include grow lights, climate control, growing media, fertilisers and nutrients, sold through specialty hydroponic retailers and distributors in North America and Europe. Cannabis legalisation drives demand. Listed on Nasdaq as HYFM. B2B and retail growers.

Indonesian state-owned pharmaceutical firm based in Jakarta, running pharmacy chains, clinics and labs, and making medicines. Founded in the Dutch colonial era, it is Indonesia's oldest pharma company, with manufacturing, distribution, retail pharmacies, diagnostics labs and clinics. Listed on IDX as KAEF; subsidiary of holding Bio Farma. Strong brand awareness in Indonesia with over a thousand pharmacies.

Swiss sports data and technology firm based in St Gallen supplying live data, odds, and integrity monitoring to sportsbooks and leagues, with rights deals with the NBA, NFL, UEFA and others. Customers include betting operators, media and sports bodies in dozens of countries, with revenue from data feeds, odds services and trading tools plus its Sportradar Integrity Services and Sportradar Ad:s offerings. Nasdaq listed as SRAD since 2021. B2B with strong sports industry presence.

Argentine agri-biotech from Rosario with HB4 drought-tolerant wheat and soy, bioinputs and seeds. Sells crop protection, adjuvants, biologicals and seed to farmers in Argentina, Brazil and elsewhere in South America, and has owned the Rizobacter and Pro Farm brands. Listed on NYSE as BIOX. Many South American farm customers. B2B.

Indian industrial chemicals and fertiliser group (Deepak Fertilisers, Pune/Mumbai) making ammonium nitrate, nitric acid and fertilisers for mining and farming customers. A major supplier of technical ammonium nitrate to Indian mining and explosives users, it also produces solvents and Mahadhan-branded fertilisers sold to farmers through its Smartchem unit. Part of the Deepak group. Listed on NSE and BSE. B2B.

California ophthalmology company Glaukos with the iStent micro-bypass for glaucoma, plus Photrexa for keratoconus. iStent is a tiny implant placed during cataract surgery to lower eye pressure, sold to ophthalmic surgeons worldwide; the Epi-on iLink corneal cross-linking therapy and pharmaceutical programs extend the pipeline. Based in Aliso Viejo with US and international sales. NYSE listed as GKOS. B2B.

Pennsylvania spine and orthopaedic device maker Globus Medical, NYSE listed as GMED, which merged with NuVasive in 2023. Sells implants, biologics, enabling technologies and the ExcelsiusGPS robotic navigation system to spine and orthopaedic surgeons and hospitals worldwide. Annual revenue is now in the billions of dollars after the merger. B2B with surgeon brand.

Swedish online pharmacy based in Stockholm, shipping health, beauty and OTC products to consumers. It sells prescription refills, supplements, baby and skin care products through its website and app, delivered from a large automated warehouse in Morgongava, and is among Sweden's largest online pharmacies by revenue. Private. A large consumer brand in Sweden.

Swedish pharma company in Lund (Camurus) behind long-acting injectables such as Buvidal and Brixadi for opioid dependence, using its FluidCrystal drug delivery technology. Also markets Oclaiz (CAM2029) for acromegaly and neuroendocrine tumours, selling to specialist clinicians and licensing to partners such as Braeburn for the US. Nasdaq Stockholm listed. B2B.

Paris advertising technology firm (Criteo) offering retargeting and commerce media to advertisers and publishers. It uses shopper data and AI to serve product ads across the open internet, with retailers, brands and agencies as customers and revenue largely from a share of ad spend. Operates in dozens of countries with thousands of staff. Listed on Nasdaq as CRTO. B2B with agency brand awareness.

Canadian mining drilling contractor from Moncton, New Brunswick, providing exploration drilling to mining companies worldwide. Offers surface and underground core drilling, directional and specialized drilling services for gold, copper and other mineral producers, with operations in Canada, the US, Latin America, Africa and Asia-Pacific. TSX listed as MDI. B2B.

California cybersecurity vendor (Palo Alto Networks) selling firewalls, cloud security and AI-driven security platforms to enterprises and governments globally, with tens of thousands of customers and annual revenue of about $9 billion. Platforms include Prisma Cloud, Cortex and Prisma Access, plus acquisitions such as CyberArk. Founded in 2005. Nasdaq listed as PANW. B2B with strong tech brand awareness.

Singapore luxury online marketplace (Reebonz) for pre-owned and new luxury goods; Nasdaq listed in 2018 and later delisted. Sold designer handbags, watches and fashion to consumers across Asia Pacific, with a website and app plus showrooms in Singapore and Hong Kong. Consumer brand in Asia Pacific.

New Jersey wireless spectrum company (Anterix) holding 900 MHz spectrum to give utilities private broadband networks. The firm, formerly pdvWireless, controls nationwide US licences in the band and leases capacity to electric, gas and water utilities for grid modernisation and critical communications. Nasdaq listed as ATEX. B2B, known in the utility and telecom sectors.

Tianjin CDMO (Asymchem) providing drug development and manufacturing services to global pharma. Offers process chemistry for small molecule APIs and intermediates, plus biologics and gene therapy services, with manufacturing plants in China. Customers include large multinational drugmakers under long-term contracts. Listed in Shenzhen and Hong Kong. B2B.

UK greeting card and gift retailer Card Factory with about a thousand stores, based in Wakefield. It prints and makes most of its own cards in-house at its Wakefield facility, selling them at low prices alongside balloons, gift wrap and party supplies, in stores and online (including Getting Personal). LSE listed. Consumer retail brand with high-street awareness.

California cloud security firm Qualys with vulnerability management and compliance tools, delivered as subscriptions through its Qualys Cloud Platform and its VMDR product. Customers are large enterprises, including a majority of the Forbes Global 100, and government bodies, with partners and managed security providers reselling. Founded in 1999 by Philippe Courtot. Nasdaq listed as QLYS. B2B, known in IT security circles.

IoT module and connectivity firm Telit, which merged with Thales Cinterion in 2023, supplying cellular modules to industrial and automotive customers. The combined business operates as Telit Cinterion, selling cellular IoT modules, connectivity services and the deviceWISE platform to makers of meters, vehicles, trackers and medical devices. Telit was founded in Italy and had a US base in Boca Raton. B2B.

Tel Aviv-based agrochemical company ADAMA, among the largest generic crop protection firms globally, owned by Syngenta Group and listed in Shenzhen. Sells herbicides, insecticides and fungicides to farmers through distributors in over 100 countries, with revenue of about 4 to 5 billion dollars. Formerly Makhteshim Agan, with ChemChina as the earlier parent. B2B farm input brand.

Irish-domiciled pharma Amarin, selling Vascepa, an icosapent ethyl drug for cardiovascular risk. Vascepa was approved by the FDA in 2012 and later for patients on statins with elevated triglycerides, following the REDUCE-IT outcomes trial. Sold in the US and, via partners, in Europe and elsewhere; US sales have faced generic competition. Nasdaq listed as AMRN. B2B.

Shenzhen genomics firm BGI, one of the world's largest DNA sequencing service providers, with a prominent role in genomics research and testing. Its businesses include BGI Genomics (listed in Shenzhen), sequencing instrument maker MGI Tech, and non-invasive prenatal testing sold to hospitals. Customers are research institutes, hospitals and governments worldwide. B2B and healthcare.

Hyderabad injectables maker Gland Pharma, a sterile generic injectable producer majority owned by China's Fosun. Sells to partner pharma companies in the US, Europe and other markets, which market its heparin, oncology and anaesthesia injectables under their own labels, and has expanded through the acquisition of Cenexi in France. Listed on NSE and BSE since 2020. B2B.

St Louis vegetable seed company Seminis, a global leader in vegetable seeds for fresh market growers and processors, with crops including tomatoes, peppers and cucumbers. Customers are growers and seed distributors worldwide. Monsanto acquired it in 2005 and the business now sits within Bayer. B2B agri.

Delhi NCR diagnostics chain, one of India's largest, with hundreds of labs and thousands of collection centres offering blood and imaging tests. Founded by Dr. Lal and listed on BSE/NSE (DRLAL) since a 2015 IPO. Revenue comes from test fees paid by patients and referring doctors, plus home sample collection and online booking. Consumer-facing health brand across India.

Ewing Township, New Jersey drug-delivery company known for Xyosted, a testosterone auto-injector, and Otrexup/Rasuvo methotrexate pens. It built needle-based and pen injector devices, earning revenue from product sales and licensing to pharma partners. Nasdaq-listed (ATRS); acquired by Halozyme in 2022 for around $960 million. Prescription products, little consumer brand.

Beijing insulin maker (Gan & Lee Pharmaceuticals) selling insulin analogues in China and abroad, with approval for biosimilar insulins in the US. Products include long-acting glargine and rapid-acting lispro and aspart analogues, with a partnership with Sandoz for markets outside China. Listed on Shanghai's STAR Market (603087). B2B diabetes supplier, no consumer brand.

Chandlers Ford, UK molecular diagnostics company (Novacyt) that sold COVID-19 PCR tests during the pandemic through its Primerdesign business. It also owns Lab21 and sells genetic test kits for infectious disease, with revenue falling after the COVID boom. Acquired Yourgene Health in 2023. Listed on Euronext Growth Paris and AIM London. Sells to labs and governments; low consumer awareness.

Boca Raton, Florida cannabis marketing platform offering CRM, text messaging, loyalty programs and analytics to dispensaries. Customers are cannabis retailers and brands across US states, paying monthly software subscriptions based on message volume. Went public on Nasdaq (SBIG) via SPAC in 2022. B2B SaaS to the cannabis industry.

Moscow software company founded 1991 by Boris Nuraliev, maker of 1C:Enterprise business and accounting software used by large numbers of Russian companies, and of games publishing arms. Software is sold through a network of thousands of franchised partners (1C:Franchisee) that implement and support it. Used widely by small and medium businesses and by public bodies across Russia and CIS markets. Private; revenue from licenses and partner network. Broad B2B brand in Russia.

Boston-based SEO and online marketing software maker (Semrush), selling subscription tools for keyword research, competitor analysis and content. Also offers social media, advertising and AI-visibility tools used by agencies, marketers and in-house teams, with paying customers in the tens of thousands across markets. NYSE-listed (SEMR) since 2021. Adobe agreed in late 2025 to acquire it for about $1.9 billion. Millions of users, B2B brand known in marketing circles.

San Francisco non-profit running Wikipedia and its sister projects such as Wikimedia Commons and Wiktionary, funded by donations and grants. The volunteer community writes the content in hundreds of languages, while the foundation provides servers and legal support. Hosts one of the most visited websites in the world. Global consumer brand but not-for-profit, rarely a sponsor.

Seoul mobile game publisher behind titles such as Zenonia and Baseball Superstars, sold worldwide. It earns revenue from in-app purchases in free-to-play role-playing and sports games on iOS and Android, with strong Korean and Japanese player bases. KOSDAQ-listed; acquired by Com2uS in 2019. Strong in Korean mobile gaming.

Melbourne plasma and vaccine giant (CSL) with CSL Behring (plasma therapies), Seqirus (flu vaccines) and Vifor. Operates a global network of plasma collection centres (CSL Plasma) and sells to hospitals and governments. ASX-listed (CSL), annual revenue around US$15 billion, employs about 30,000 people. A well-known healthcare brand and sports sponsor in Australia.

West Lafayette, Indiana targeted radiopharma biotech whose PSMA-targeted work became Pluvicto after Novartis acquired it. Endocyte developed small-molecule drug conjugates that deliver cancer drugs to cells carrying folate and PSMA receptors, including vintafolide. Novartis bought it in 2018 for about $2.1 billion. Prescription pharma, B2B.

Israeli fuel and energy group (Paz Oil) running the largest network of gas stations and Yellow convenience stores in Israel, plus a refinery in Ashdod. Also sells fuel and lubricants to industry and has a growing natural gas business. Listed on Tel Aviv Stock Exchange. High consumer visibility in Israel.

Osaka ophthalmic pharma leader (Santen) with eye drops for glaucoma and dry eye, including Tapcom, Diquas and Cyclokat. Customers are eye doctors and patients, and it holds a leading position in Japan and parts of Asia and Europe. Tokyo-listed (4536), selling in 60+ countries. Prescription brand with some consumer awareness.

San Diego flavor ingredient developer that found sweet and salt taste enhancers sold to food makers like PepsiCo. Revenue came from royalties and research fees from customers including Nestle, Coca-Cola and Firmenich. Built on screening human taste receptors. Nasdaq-listed (SNMX); acquired by Firmenich in 2018. B2B ingredients.

Boston sports-nutrition company behind HotShot, a drink for relieving muscle cramps popular with athletes. Developed with Nobel laureate Rod MacKinnon, it uses a TRP-channel activating formula (ginger, cinnamon and capsaicin). Sold online and in sporting goods stores, with endurance athletes and sports teams as core users. Nasdaq-listed (FLKS); merged with Salarius in 2019, ending the consumer line. Strongest sports link in this batch.

London local government body for the Square Mile, running the financial district, Guildhall, markets and the Barbican. Also owns Smithfield, Billingsgate and Spitalfields markets, Tower Bridge, and Epping Forest. It is funded by property income, business rates and the City's Cash endowment. A public authority, not a commercial brand.
